newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN BOSS BECKENBAUER DEMANDS IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN BOSS BECKENBAUER DEMANDS IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Bayern Munich chairman Franz Beckenbauer has told his players that they will have to stop acting like prima donnas if they want to win a record 14th German championship when the season resumes at the weekend.

The former World Cup-winning coach and captain was very critical of the team's football in the first half of the season despite the fact they went into the two-month winter break in December at the top of the table.
Beckenbauer wants an improvement in performance both on and off the pitch. Trivial individual battles must stop if Bayern are to end Borussia Dortmund's grip on the Bundesliga.
"They must learn that they are not so important," Beckenbauer said.

One of the most prominent reported disagreements at Bayern in recent seasons has been between Germany captain and striker Juergen Klinsmann and veteran ex-international and World Cup captain Lothar Matthaeus.
Coach Giovanni Trapattoni says the club's two biggest names have settled their differences. But the Italian also believes that attitudes have to change in the second half of the season.
"In Germany there is the idea that the most prominent player must do everything. Why is that?" he said. "Every player has a precise role to play. There are 11 men in the collective unit.
"But when I say the word 'collective' to the lads, they look at me with almost disbelief. Perhaps it's because they all feel they have to be the best player on the pitch. That's wrong."

Bayern, who have a two-point lead over reigning champions Borussia Dortmund as they bid for their first championship since 1994, begin their campaign with a home game against lowly St Pauli on Saturday.

European Cup quarter-finalists Dortmund, who struggled with injuries in the first half of the season, re-start their campaign with an almost completely fit squad and a big match at home to third-placed Bayer Leverkusen on Friday.

Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld, who has led Dortmund to the title in the last two seasons, is in no doubt about the immense task against Leverkusen. But he believes the main challenge will come from Bayern before the season finishes at the end of May.
"It's an absolute cracker of a game. It's as big as any European game as far as Dortmund is concerned," he said.

"There is going to be a battle between four clubs at the top (Bayern, Dortmund, Leverkusen and VfB Stuttgart). I expect Bayern to provide the main challenge. After missing out on two championships they are under more pressure than us."
Fourth-placed Stuttgart, who played some of the most attractive football in the first half, begin their campaign with an awkward trip to eighth-placed Schalke on Saturday.
